summary.text: Gilda Cobb-Hunter is a Democratic state representative from Orangeburg who represents South Carolina House District 95 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026.

A social work administrator and former House minority leader, she is first vice chairman of the Ways and Means Committee, and according to Ballotpedia she is the only candidate listed in the general election.

paragraphs.text: Gilda Cobb-Hunter was born on November 5, 1952, in Gifford, Florida, and earned a B.S. from Florida A&M University in 1973 and an M.A. from Florida State University in 1978, according to the House member page.
The page lists her as a licensed independent social worker since 1990 and a member of the South Carolina chapter of the National Association of Social Workers.
Cobb-Hunter served as House minority leader from 1997 to 2000 and is a graduate of Leadership South Carolina, Class of 1986, according to the House member page.
The page also lists her as a Democratic National Committee national committeewoman and a past president of the National Black Caucus of State Legislators.
Her committee assignment is Ways and Means, where she is first vice chairman.
Ballotpedia reports that she was one of South Carolina's six superdelegates to the 2016 Democratic National Convention.
